explain.summary: 8.8% is the simulated chance that at least one of 25 entries wins all 18 remaining picks. Simulated one at a time the entries survive about 0.55% each, which would give 12.8% if they were independent; they share teams and die together, so it lands at 8.8%. Expected survivors 0.14 is the same simulation counted per entry. The per-pick numbers in the plans are the planning view, discounted 16x for later weeks, so the product of a plan's picks is far below its simulated survival.
explain.exposure: 25 live entries across 5 teams; 12 on LAC. The board has 2 teams at 75% or better, then it drops to 72% (a 5% step after the top two). The objective is that at least one entry survives the season, so entries only spread onto weaker teams when that costs little; moving a dozen entries onto a 64% team to avoid sharing would lower that probability. The flip side is correlation: if ARI wins, the 12 LAC entries go out together.

Road pick BAL: the line already includes home field (about 1.6 points), so the probability is not optimistic about it.
Week 18 spots are shrunk toward 50% (19% flatter) and given extra variance because clinched teams rest starters.

Every percentage for a later week on this page is the planning view: the projection's uncertainty is inflated 16x (backtest-tuned), which pulls distant games toward 50% so a sure thing now beats a slightly better projection months away. The survival percentages are simulated with calibrated uncertainty instead.
A tie counts as a loss, and later weeks of every plan are re-optimised on each run; only this week's pick is a recommendation.
